hypotheses.justification: The proof only needs `Function.Injective (dualCotangentMap f.hom)`, which it gets from the bijectivity lemma `dualCotangentMap_bijective_of_etaleKernel`. The isogeny hypothesis (through `finrank_lie_eq`) is used there only for surjectivity. Injectivity follows from `hker` alone. `TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.algebraEtale_quotient_kernelHopfIdeal_iff [Algebra.FiniteType k K] (f : H ⟶ K)` (HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Etale.lean) says that `Algebra.Etale k (K ⧸ ker)` is equivalent to `Function.Injective (derivationCompLieHom (B := k) f.hom)`. It needs no isogeny and no smoothness. `Algebra.FiniteType k K` comes from `[Algebra.Smooth k K]`, since smooth includes finite presentation, and Mathlib has the instance from finite presentation to finite type. Proof of injectivity: suppose `dualCotangentMap f.hom x = dualCotangentMap f.hom y`. Apply `cotangentLinearEquiv (A := H)` and rewrite with `Derivation.cotangentLinearEquiv_dualCotangentMap`. This gives `derivationComp f.hom (e_K x) = derivationComp f.hom (e_K y)`, which is `derivationCompLieHom f.hom` applied to both sides (`derivationCompLieHom_apply`). Injectivity of that map gives `e_K x = e_K y`, so `x = y`. This is the same pattern as the proof of `BialgHom.dualCotangentMap_injective_of_surjective`. Then `f.hom.dualCotangentMap_mem_adjointWeightSpace_iff_of_injective` closes the goal. `hf` appears nowhere else in the statement. This deletion is independent of the `[Algebra.Smooth k H]` deletion; both can be removed together.

The statement never mentions this instance. It is used only inside `dualCotangentMap_bijective_of_etaleKernel`, through `finrank_lie_eq`, to get surjectivity of the differential. The theorem only needs injectivity. As explained for `hf`, injectivity follows from `algebraEtale_quotient_kernelHopfIdeal_iff`, which needs only `[Algebra.FiniteType k K]` (supplied by `[Algebra.Smooth k K]`), together with `Derivation.cotangentLinearEquiv_dualCotangentMap`. Then `BialgHom.dualCotangentMap_mem_adjointWeightSpace_iff_of_injective` applies, and it has no smoothness assumptions. So `omit [Algebra.Smooth k H] in` leaves a true and provable theorem.
